chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from al-Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: The moon was eclipsed, so my father went out, and I went out with him to al-Masjid al-Haram. Then he prayed eight rak'ahs, praying as one normally prays a rak'ah and two sajdahs.

So these two reports agree with the doctrines of the 'ammah, while practice is based on the first two reports, because they agree with the narrations that contain the detailed description of Salat al-Kusuf. We have cited them in our major book, and the entire group acts upon them.

key_terms.الْعِصَابَةِ: the collective body of the Imami companions/scholars

ai.seo_question: Which hadiths are relied upon for determining the number of rak'ahs in Salat al-Kusuf?
ai.summary: This report discusses the number of rak'ahs in Salat al-Kusuf and then states that certain reports are set aside because they conform to the views of the 'ammah, while reliance is placed on the earlier reports that give the detailed ruling. It reflects a jurisprudential method of preferring reports supported by more detailed narrations and the practice of the Imami community.
